node_definition.done_when: A test in tests/test_a_session_live_read_writes_nothing.py has two arms. The read-only arm builds a fixture crew home holding follower registrations, a dead local lease and a seat, makes every file mode 0444 and every directory mode 0555, then sets the seat to mode 000 after that sweep so the unreadable-seat branch is exercised; it calls the live view with session= and asserts the fixture's runs come back with no error and the home's tree is byte-identical afterwards. The writable arm holds a dead local lease on a normal writable home and asserts a live read reports the lease stale and leaves its file in place, so catching OSError in release_holder alone does not pass. _fresh_watch_holder in reckon/crew/watch_unit.py is where the read path calls release_holder, so the read path stops calling it there; registration and lease release on a writable home outside a read keep their behaviour. Both arms fail at the base. Negative control: restoring the a+b open in _follower_liveness raises a permission error on the 0444 registration and the test fails; every log, the negative control's included, is written under the run directory. Gate: tests/test_a_session_live_read_writes_nothing.py tests/test_live_view_reads_under_a_read_only_home.py tests/test_crew_watch_visibility.py tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py. baseline_suite and after_suite are run with the project's armed suite command, PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_a_session_live_read_writes_nothing.py, at the base and at the head, each log naming its revision, tree and literal command and ending EXIT=. Every test file that imports a production module the node changed adds no failure against a base arm: run both arms from git archive extractions on node-local disk with the main checkout's .env linked, record both logs, and re-run any id that differs between arms serially three times on each revision. ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the staged paths. Run the gate in the foreground on the fleet allocation.
